_doc: Scenario cases for the made-up organization Kestrel Bay Group (docs/phase7-prompt.md T6 item 1; docs/decisions.md 2026-10-20). Each scenario is a barrier THEME from a published accessibility progress report, written again in our own words: no passage is copied, no figure is taken over, no real person is described and no real organization is a tenant. db/seed.ts creates the cases in this order through the frozen core (createCase, transition), so case N gets ref BAR-000N and the seed stops if a ref differs. The staff case page and /sources read this file (lib/scenarios.ts). 'sources' lists every report we tried to read on 2026-10-20, including the ones we could not reach or did not use.

org.name: Kestrel Bay Group
org.about: A made-up federally regulated group with a bank, an airline and offices, so that one demo organization can hold barriers from every kind of report we read.

sources.title: 2024 Health Canada Accessibility Progress Report

scenarios.theme: The phone line hangs up while a caller types a card number
scenarios.text: When I call to check my balance, the phone system asks me to type my card number. I need more time to find the keys, and it hangs up before I finish. This keeps happening.
scenarios.summary: The phone line hangs up before you can finish typing your card number.
scenarios.publicSummary: The phone line ended calls before callers who need more time could finish entering a card number.

scenarios.theme: Card number and phone number printed too small and flat to read
scenarios.text: Letter: The numbers on my new card are tiny and flat. With my low vision I cannot read the card number or the phone number on the back, and I cannot feel them either.
scenarios.summary: The card number and phone number on the new card are too small and flat to read.
scenarios.publicSummary: The card number and phone number on a payment card were printed too small and flat for people with low vision.

scenarios.theme: No seating in the branch line, and accessible parking is often full
scenarios.text: There is nowhere to sit while I wait in line at the branch, and I cannot stand for long. The accessible parking spaces out front are almost always full.
scenarios.summary: The branch has no seating in the waiting line, and its accessible parking is often full.
scenarios.publicSummary: A branch had no seating for people waiting in line and too few accessible parking spaces.

scenarios.theme: The phone menu needs key presses, and a live agent is hard to reach
scenarios.text: Your phone menu only works with key presses. My hands shake, so I often press the wrong number and end up back at the start. I could not reach a real person.
scenarios.summary: The phone menu needs key presses that are hard with shaking hands, and you could not reach a person.
scenarios.publicSummary: The phone menu worked only with key presses and made it hard to reach a live agent.

scenarios.theme: Documents and forms posted as PDFs that screen readers cannot read
scenarios.text: The forms on your website are scanned PDFs. My screen reader reads nothing on them, so I cannot fill them in. Please post a web form or an accessible version.
scenarios.summary: The website's forms are scanned PDFs that a screen reader can't read.
scenarios.publicSummary: Forms were posted as scanned PDFs that screen readers could not read.

scenarios.theme: Identity checks only by voice call, with no text option for Deaf customers
scenarios.text: I am Deaf. To unlock my online banking, the only way to prove who I am was a voice phone call. Please give me a way to do it by text or chat.
scenarios.summary: The identity check to unlock online banking was only a voice call, which does not work for a Deaf customer.
scenarios.publicSummary: Identity checks to unlock online banking offered only a voice call, with no text-based option for Deaf, deafened and hard of hearing customers.

scenarios.theme: Read aloud works only on sent chat messages
scenarios.text: In the work chat tool, Read Aloud only works on a message after I send it. I need to hear my message while I write it, so I can catch mistakes before anyone sees them.
scenarios.summary: The chat tool's Read Aloud feature works only after a message is sent, not while writing.
scenarios.publicSummary: A chat tool's read-aloud feature worked only on sent messages, not while writing one.

scenarios.theme: A motion-sensor entrance door does not open reliably
scenarios.text: The motion-sensor door at the main office entrance often does not open when I come up to it in my wheelchair. I wait or ask someone. A push-button opener would work every time.
scenarios.summary: The motion-sensor entrance door often does not open for wheelchair users.
scenarios.publicSummary: A motion-sensor entrance door did not open reliably for people using wheelchairs.

scenarios.theme: The accessibility discount's rules and form are hard to find and understand
scenarios.text: I tried to apply for the accessibility discount on your website. I could not understand who can get it, and I could not find the form. I gave up.
scenarios.summary: The accessibility discount's rules were hard to understand and its application form was hard to find.
scenarios.publicSummary: The rules and the application form for an accessibility discount were hard to find and understand.

scenarios.theme: Video meetings are hard to join from some meeting rooms
scenarios.text: In some of our meeting rooms I cannot join the video meeting with live captions turned on, and the room camera cannot show the sign language interpreter. I use captions for every meeting.
scenarios.summary: In some meeting rooms, you can't join video meetings with captions, and the camera can't show the interpreter.
scenarios.publicSummary: Some meeting rooms did not support joining video meetings with captions or showing a sign language interpreter.

scenarios.theme: A long wait for booked wheelchair assistance at the airport
scenarios.text: I booked wheelchair help for my flight. At the airport I waited a long time before anyone came, and I almost missed my connection. Nobody could tell me how long it would be.
scenarios.summary: Booked wheelchair assistance at the airport took so long that you almost missed a connection.
scenarios.publicSummary: Passengers who booked wheelchair assistance at the airport waited a long time for help.

scenarios.theme: Too few quiet spaces after the return to the office
scenarios.text: Employee said that since staff came back to the office, there are almost no quiet rooms to work in. As an autistic employee, the noise on the open floor makes it very hard to focus.
scenarios.summary: Since the return to the office, there are too few quiet rooms for an autistic employee to focus.
scenarios.publicSummary: After the return to the office, there were too few quiet, private spaces for neurodivergent employees.

scenarios.theme: A power wheelchair does not fit the cargo door of a smaller aircraft
scenarios.text: Caller said nobody told them when they booked that their power wheelchair would not fit through the cargo door of the smaller plane on their second flight. They found out at the gate.
scenarios.summary: Nobody said at booking that the power wheelchair would not fit the smaller plane's cargo door.
scenarios.publicSummary: A customer learned at the gate that their power wheelchair would not fit the cargo door of a smaller aircraft.

scenarios.theme: Gate screens that do not show announcements as text
scenarios.text: Gate changes were only announced over the speakers. I am hard of hearing and the screen at my gate did not show the change, so I almost missed my flight.
scenarios.summary: A gate change was only announced out loud and not shown on the gate screen.
